newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank relaxes forex forward trading.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank relaxes forex forward trading.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Thursday it would lift all current restrictions on the types of income that can be used for foreign exchange forward trading.

The liberalisation, effective December 16, means investors will be able to conduct trading on three now-restricted items -- income from work or services rendered, income from money tranfers and money earmarked for remittance abroad.
"This latest liberalisation should have a positive effect on the forward foreign exchange market," the central bank said in a statement.
The bank on January 4 relaxed a restriction that allowed only exporters, importers and transport and insurance firms to conduct forward trading.
The January reform abolished a requirement that customers had to deposit three percent of a forward contract's value with banks, instead allowing customers to negotiate deposits with banks.
The length of contracts was increased to one year from six months in January.
